title: Why Modern Cars Are DESIGNED to Crumple 💥🚗 #shorts

scenes.text: Cars are built to crush. That's what saves you.
In a crash, your speed must drop to zero. Stretch that stop over more time and the force on you shrinks. Twice the time, about half the force.
Béla Barényi patented it for Mercedes in nineteen fifty-two: crush zones front and rear, around a rigid passenger cage.
The nineteen fifty-nine Fintail was the first Mercedes built that way.
Electric cars shift the puzzle. No engine block can free up front space, though Ford said its Mach-E got about ten percent less.
The new job: guard the battery in the floor, with strong side sills that steer crash forces around it.
A crumpled hood isn't a failure. It took the hit so you didn't. Follow EV Drive.
